chat_name: Memo: Northwind credit memo / Checklist consolidation
prompt:
UNDERWRITER TO COMPLETE CHECKLIST: 42 items in the memo, 38 after grouping by code.

Group: Documents to request
1. (Section 2) **Waiver.** The waiver document W-25-0388 and its terms; Credit Administration records would normally contain it.
2. (Section 2) **Gaps.** Management biographies beyond the D5 ¶5 notes; competitor and market position information (would normally come from the bank's licensed industry research feed); and any customer or product mix beyond D1 §5 and D5 ¶1.
3. (Section 5) Collateral values (accounts receivable aging, inventory balances at cost, equipment values). A field exam, appraisal or Borrowing Base Certificate would normally contain these.
4. (Section 5) The December 31, 2025 Borrowing Base Certificate and any more recent monthly certificates, and so FY2025 and current revolver availability and Excess Availability. Credit Administration is to attach the December 31, 2025 certificate [D1, §2 Footnote *].
5. (Section 5) Schedule 1.1 (Eligible Inventory definition) and any reserves established by the Lender. The full Credit Agreement would contain these.
6. (Section 5) The guaranty document itself (terms, scope, any financial covenants), and the guarantor's financial statements, net worth and liquidity. The guaranty agreement and a personal financial statement would normally contain these.
7. (Section 5) The landlord waiver terms, the lease term and rent, and the Ostrander Properties, LLC relationship to the guarantor. The lease and waiver documents would normally contain these.
8. (Section 5) Lien perfection evidence (UCC searches, filings), deposit account control agreements, and the purchase-money Lien balance (relevant to the $500,000 limit in D2 §7.5(b)(iii)). Legal or Credit Administration files would normally contain these.
9. (Section 5) The balance and terms of the capital leases against vehicle values, and the Ridgeway Truck Finance lease documents.

Group: Conflicts to resolve
10. (Sections 3, 6) **CONFLICT:** FY2025 EBITDA is 4,100 [D1, Table 1] against "about $4.5 million" [D1, §6]. Reconcile before use. No value has been chosen. Also cited in the repeats: [D1, Table 1: EBITDA, FY2025]

Group: Policy items for judgment
11. (Section 6) **Applicability:** Decide whether Policy §4.2 applies to this annual review, and whether it is a "renewal" or "new-money request." Policy and legal may need to confirm.
12. (Section 6) **Exception determination:** Decide whether any exception exists under §4.2.1 or §4.2.2, whether §4.2.3(c) is triggered, and whether Chief Credit Officer or Senior Loan Committee approval is needed.

Group: Sections to write
13. (Sections 2, 3, 6) **Customer concentration (policy).** D4 §4.2.4 requires the memo to address customer concentration in Section 7 if any single customer exceeds 25% of revenue in the most recent fiscal year. [D4, §4.2.4] The underwriter should determine how this applies to the 23% figure in D1 §5. Also cited in the repeats: [D1, §5] [D1, §5; D4, §4.2.4]
14. (Section 3) **3.5:** Underwriter Commentary is reserved for the underwriter.

Group: Other checks
15. (Section 1) Header fields: Underwriter, Senior reviewer and Date.
16. (Section 1) Whether the review includes a renewal, extension or amendment request. Both the Term Loan balance and the Revolving Commitment fall due December 15, 2027 [D2, §2.1(a)-(b)], and D5 ¶5 records only that no change to the facility was requested. The request type label above is taken from D5 and should be confirmed.
17. (Section 1) Any "Request type" wording the bank's template convention requires.
18. (Sections 2, 6) **Change of control (legal review).** D2 §7.6 provides: "It shall be an Event of Default if the members of the Borrower on the Closing Date cease to control the Borrower, or if Dale Ostrander ceases to have primary responsibility for the operations of the Borrower and a successor reasonably satisfactory to the Lender is not appointed within a reasonable period." [D2, §7.6] The following terms are quoted but not interpreted here: Also cited in the repeats: [D5, ¶5]
19. (Section 2) "control"
20. (Section 2) "primary responsibility for the operations"
21. (Section 2) "reasonably satisfactory"
22. (Section 2) "a reasonable period" Refer to the underwriter and legal how these terms apply to the CEO transition and the possible ESOP sale described in D5 ¶5.
23. (Section 3) **FY2025 revolver availability and liquidity:** the December 31, 2025 Borrowing Base Certificate is needed [D1, §2 Footnote *]. Excess Availability against the $1,000,000 minimum [D2, §7.3] is not reported in the certificates [D1, §7].
24. (Section 3) **Debt service definition:** the spread labels debt service "(P+I)" [D1, §2 Definitions]. The agreement's definition includes interest on the Revolving Loans [D2, §1.1]. The documents do not state whether the spread debt service includes revolver interest. Confirm with Credit Analysis.
25. (Section 3) **Quarterly source basis:** Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 figures come from internally prepared statements, not audited ones [D1, §3 Note to Table 3].
26. (Section 3) **3.4:** pro forma figures are not applicable on the documents provided, because no facility change is proposed. Confirm whether any pro forma presentation is wanted.
27. (Section 4) Resolve the FY2025 EBITDA conflict (4,100 in D1 Table 1 against "about $4.5 million" in D1 §6) and confirm which figure the FY2025 compliance certificate used.
28. (Section 4) Obtain the Borrowing Base Certificates and confirm Excess Availability against §7.3, including whether the December 31, 2025 certificate was delivered.
29. (Section 4) Review the definitional alignment between the spread and the agreement. The spread labels its row "Unfunded capex" and "Cash taxes," while D2 uses "Unfinanced Capital Expenditures" and "cash taxes paid (including Permitted Tax Distributions)." [D1, Table 1]. [D2, §1.1]. The spread says its Cash taxes row shows tax distributions. [D1, header]. D1 does not state whether the Debt service (P+I) row includes revolver interest, which D2 §1.1 requires.
30. (Section 4) Refer the following §7.6 wording to the underwriter and legal. I have not interpreted it: "cease to control," "primary responsibility for the operations," "successor reasonably satisfactory to the Lender," and "within a reasonable period." Legal should also advise on how the planned CEO transition and the ESOP discussion relate to these terms. [D5, ¶5].
31. (Section 4) Refer to legal the scope of "purchase-money Liens" and "Liens securing Capital Lease Obligations, limited to the vehicles and equipment subject to those leases" under §7.5(b).
32. (Section 4) Decide whether to carry the W-25-0388 waiver into the memo narrative and how to treat it.
33. (Section 4) Provide any covenant-headroom analysis. I have not calculated any.
34. (Section 5) Legal and underwriter review of the following terms in D2 §7.6, which are quoted and not interpreted: "control," "primary responsibility for the operations," "a successor reasonably satisfactory to the Lender," and "a reasonable period." Whether a transition to Megan Ostrander-Kolb or a sale of up to 30% of the membership interests to an ESOP engages §7.6, and how either affects the guaranty, is a question for the underwriter and legal.
35. (Section 5) Legal and underwriter review of the "reasonable credit judgment" standard for Borrowing Base reserves in D2 §1.1.
36. (Section 5) Underwriter to confirm whether the Excess Availability covenant (D2 §7.3) is tested, since the compliance certificates do not report it [D1, §7].
37. (Section 6) **Pro forma figures:** Pro forma total leverage and pro forma DSCR at origination (Section 3.4) are not stated in the provided documents. Their source would be the underwriter's pro forma analysis or the spread.
38. (Section 6) **Missing availability data:** The December 31, 2025 Borrowing Base Certificate and the Excess Availability figures against the $1,000,000 minimum are not in the provided documents. Credit Administration would normally hold them.
